sentences.text:
HYDER ALI AGED 33 YEARS S/O.BAKKER, THAIKKOOTTATHIL HOUSE,
 AYYOTTICHIRA DESOM, VELIYAMKODU VILLAGE MALAPPURAM DISTRICT, , PIN -  676553 RESPONDENT:
 STATE OF KERALA REPRESENTED BY THE INSPECTOR OF POLICE, VADEKKEKAD  POLICE STATION, THROUGH THE PUBLIC PROSECUTOR, HIGH COURT OF KERALA,
 ERNAKULAM, , PIN - 682031  Application praying that in the circumstances stated therein the High Court be pleased to suspend the sentence in S.C.No.898 of 2023 on the file of Court of Special Judge, Fast Track Special Court, Kunnamkulam (Thrissur Sessions Division), pending appeal and to grant bail to the applicant.

This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application and upon hearing the arguments of DINESH MATHEW J.MURICKEN,
VINOD S. PILLAI, MOHAMMED THAYIB N.M., NAYANA VARGHESE, RIA VARGHESE,
JERRY PETER, Advocates for the petitioner and of the PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the respondent, the Court passed the following:
 C.S.SUDHA, J.
 --------------------------------------------------------------
 Crl.M.Appl. No.1 of 2024  in  Crl. Appeal No.2308 of 2024  ---------------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 10th day of January 2025  ORDER

This is an application filed under Section 430(1) of the Bharathiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,
seeking suspension of sentence of the applicant/accused in S.C. No.898 of 2023 on the file of the Court of Session, Thrissur.

The applicant/accused has been found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 376 (1) IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years and to a fine of 50,000/-.
2. The learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that PW1, the victim, does not have a consistent version.

In the FIS, her version is that the accused came to her residence, they had a conversation for some time and thereafter the accused raped her whereas in her testimony she deposed that the accused trespassed into her house and committed the offence.

Therefore, in the Hyder Ali vs State Of Kerala on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190759266/
1 light of the inconsistent versions, the argument is that the accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt.

sentences.text: 3. Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor opposes the application and submits that the evidence on record is more than sufficient to establish the offence alleged against him and there is nothing to disbelieve the victim in this case.
The learned Public Prosecutor also submits that there is medical evidence to substantiate the offence.
However, on instructions, she submits that the accused has no criminal antecedents.

5. Taking into account the fact that the applicant/accused has been convicted only for a period of seven years and as there is no possibility of the appeal being taken up in the near future, in the interest of justice, the substantive sentence of imprisonment imposed on the applicant/accused is suspended till the disposal of the appeal subject to the following conditions:-
i) The applicant/accused shall be released on bail on executing a bond for 50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial court;
ii) He shall deposit the entire fine amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
iii) He shall not commit any offence(s) while on bail;
iv) The applicant/accused shall not in any way contact or attempt to contact the victim or her family member(s) in any manner;
v) If the conviction and sentence of the applicant/accused is upheld or even modified,
the time during which he is so released shall be excluded in computing the term of his sentence as provided in Section 430(4) BNSS.
vi) It is also made clear that if any of the conditions are violated, the bail shall stand cancelled.
Post on 21/03/2025.
Sd/-
C.S.SUDHA NP JUDGE 10-01-2025 /True Copy/
